title: Shell command injection
why_it_matters: Untrusted arguments passed to a shell can change the command being executed and cause unintended actions.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker supplies shell metacharacters or additional commands through a tool argument that is interpolated into a shell invocation.
remediation: Avoid shell invocation; use a fixed executable with validated argument arrays and strict input validation.

title: Tool description poisoning
why_it_matters: A tool description is part of the context used by an AI agent and can steer it toward unsafe actions.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker embeds misleading or manipulative directions in a tool description so an agent misuses the tool or conceals its behavior.
remediation: Keep descriptions factual, review changes, and treat tool-provided instructions as untrusted data.

title: Instruction override
why_it_matters: Instructions embedded in tool content may conflict with the user's intent or the agent's governing instructions.
how_attackers_use_it: A description tells the agent to disregard prior instructions, hide actions, or disclose information.
remediation: Remove instruction-like text from tool descriptions and isolate untrusted content from trusted instructions.

title: Hidden Unicode in descriptions
why_it_matters: Invisible or direction-changing characters can disguise text from reviewers while remaining present to downstream consumers.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker inserts zero-width or bidirectional control characters to conceal malicious instructions or alter how text is displayed.
remediation: Reject unexpected control and format characters, and render descriptions in a way that exposes invisible characters during review.

title: Exfiltration through attacker-controlled URLs
why_it_matters: Sending sensitive values to a caller-controlled destination can disclose data outside the intended trust boundary.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker supplies a URL or destination that causes the tool to transmit user data to an untrusted endpoint.
remediation: Use allowlisted destinations, avoid placing sensitive values in URLs, and validate both scheme and host.

title: Sensitive file access
why_it_matters: Broad file access can expose credentials, private configuration, or user data to a tool caller.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker requests files outside the intended application data set using a path accepted without an adequate allowlist.
remediation: Restrict access to an explicit root and allowlisted files, and enforce permissions independently of caller input.

title: Path traversal
why_it_matters: Traversal sequences can escape an intended directory boundary and reach unrelated files.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker provides relative path components or alternate path encodings to access paths outside the permitted root.
remediation: Canonicalize paths, verify the resolved path remains under an allowlisted root, and reject traversal forms.

title: Arbitrary file write or delete
why_it_matters: Unrestricted writes or deletes can corrupt data, remove user files, or change application behavior.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker selects an unintended path or content to overwrite or remove files through a powerful tool.
remediation: Limit operations to an allowlisted workspace, require narrowly scoped paths, and apply safeguards for destructive changes.

title: Server-side request forgery
why_it_matters: A server that fetches caller-selected destinations may reach internal services that are not exposed to the caller.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker makes a network-capable tool request local, private, or otherwise unintended destinations.
remediation: Use destination allowlists, block private and local address ranges after resolution, and constrain redirects and schemes.

title: Context stuffing with long descriptions
why_it_matters: Excessive tool metadata can crowd out relevant context and make malicious or important content harder to review.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker adds irrelevant or repetitive text to consume context and obscure instructions or tool behavior.
remediation: Keep descriptions concise, enforce reasonable size limits, and review unusually large metadata.

title: Tool behavior rug pull
why_it_matters: A previously reviewed tool may become unsafe if its description or behavior changes after approval.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker changes a tool after it is trusted, relying on stale approval or cached metadata to avoid scrutiny.
remediation: Pin and verify tool metadata, surface changes for re-approval, and monitor behavior against reviewed versions.

title: Tool shadowing
why_it_matters: A similarly named tool can be mistaken for a trusted tool and receive sensitive arguments or authority.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker registers a lookalike tool name or description that competes with a trusted tool during selection.
remediation: Use clear provenance and namespaces, detect name collisions, and display the server identity with tool choices.

title: Confused deputy
why_it_matters: A tool may use its own authority on behalf of a caller who should not have that authority.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker persuades a privileged tool to perform an action against a resource the caller could not access directly.
remediation: Bind authorization to the user and requested resource, apply least privilege, and verify intent at the point of action.

title: Prompt injection through tool output
why_it_matters: Tool results can contain attacker-controlled text that influences later agent decisions.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker places instructions in retrieved content or a remote response that the agent later treats as trusted guidance.
remediation: Treat tool output as untrusted data, separate it from instructions, and require confirmation for consequential actions.

title: Over-permissioned tool
why_it_matters: Excessive permissions increase the impact of mistakes, compromised inputs, and malicious instructions.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker exploits a broad capability to perform actions beyond what the task requires.
remediation: Split broad tools into narrow operations and grant only the minimum resource and action permissions needed.

title: Unvalidated SQL input
why_it_matters: Interpolating untrusted values into SQL can change query meaning and expose or modify data.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker crafts input that alters a dynamically constructed database query.
remediation: Use parameterized queries, validate input, and restrict database permissions to the operation required.

title: Secrets embedded in descriptions
why_it_matters: Tool descriptions may be exposed to clients, logs, or model context and are not a safe place for credentials.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker or accidental change places a token or credential in metadata that is broadly distributed.
remediation: Remove credentials from descriptions, rotate exposed secrets, and retrieve secrets through a protected mechanism.

title: Unrestricted network access
why_it_matters: Unrestricted outbound connectivity can enable data disclosure or access to unintended services.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker directs a network-capable tool to arbitrary hosts or protocols.
remediation: Restrict egress to required destinations and protocols, and validate destinations before connecting.

title: Unrestricted URL parameter
why_it_matters: A caller-controlled URL can expose the server to untrusted content and unintended network destinations.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker selects a URL that causes the tool to fetch or transmit data to an unexpected service.
remediation: Prefer fixed destinations or strict allowlists and validate URL scheme, host, and resolved address.

title: Arbitrary file write through path input
why_it_matters: A writable path controlled by a caller can target files outside the intended workspace.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker supplies a path that resolves to a sensitive or executable file and writes attacker-chosen content.
remediation: Resolve and constrain write paths to an approved root, and avoid overwriting existing files without authorization.

title: Arbitrary file deletion
why_it_matters: A deletion capability can cause irreversible data loss when the target is not tightly scoped.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker names an important file or directory as the deletion target through a permissive tool.
remediation: Constrain targets, validate ownership and scope, and use confirmation or recoverable deletion for sensitive operations.

title: Hidden AI-directed content
why_it_matters: Instructions hidden in markup or metadata may be overlooked in ordinary review but still reach an agent.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker embeds directives in comments, hidden blocks, or formatting that a consumer may process despite visual concealment.
remediation: Strip or expose hidden markup, inspect normalized content, and keep machine-consumed metadata reviewable.

title: Untrusted content passed to a command
why_it_matters: Command construction from untrusted data can turn a narrow operation into arbitrary command execution.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker supplies metacharacters or crafted arguments that are interpreted by a shell or downstream command.
remediation: Do not build shell strings from caller input; use argument arrays and validate each argument against the expected format.

title: Data disclosure through remote fetch
why_it_matters: A tool that combines sensitive data with an uncontrolled network request can disclose information to third parties.
how_attackers_use_it: An attacker causes selected data to be included in a request sent to an endpoint they control.
remediation: Do not send secrets to caller-controlled destinations, minimize transmitted data, and enforce destination allowlists.
